contract.skin.1: The page root, above the wallpaper and below the content. Use its pseudo-elements for ambient effects.
contract.skin.2: All light glass cards, from compact data rows to full panels. **Do not use `inset box-shadow` for the inner ring**: inset shadows render **below child elements**, so any filled header or row can cover part of the ring (observed on the push-history table header on 2026-08-24). For a ring **above the content**, use `outline` with a negative `outline-offset`. It renders last, stays visible and follows the corner radius. A border is also safe for the outer ring: children stay inside the padding box.
contract.skin.3: Strong glass surfaces: popovers, floating bars and drawers. As with glass, use outline for the inner ring, not an inset shadow.
contract.skin.4: All buttons. These are short elements, so pill-shaped corners are safe.
contract.skin.5: Primary buttons, normally with a solid pink background.
contract.skin.6: Destructive buttons (delete / destroy), also marked btn. **Without this rule, “Confirm destruction” can look identical to “Confirm”**: the solid variant also has btn-primary and inherits its color, losing the red warning. The other two variants use red text and borders, which a btn border can cover. A background/border/color rule is enough. Keep it less prominent than the primary action: it should encourage a pause, not a click.
contract.skin.7: Inputs, textareas and selects. **Use `:focus-within`, not `:focus`**: the single-line input hook is on a non-focusable **wrapper div**, so `:focus` never matches (it is accepted but has no effect). Bare textarea/select elements also match `:focus-within`, covering both forms with one rule.
contract.skin.9: Page navigation container. Used by horizontal tab bars and **vertical section lists**; do not style every instance as a horizontal bar.
contract.skin.12: Non-interactive badges: header status pills such as “Server running”, and compact inline counts/tags such as the 3 in “Subscriptions 3”. **Do not add hover styles**. Backgrounds usually carry semantic meaning (platform or push-type colors, often inline); overriding them can misrepresent state. Prefer outlines and shadows. **One hook, two shapes**: header pills have padding, inline badges rely on line height with no vertical space. Use outline with a negative offset; a border adds 2px and shifts the row. **Do not outline in the same color**: the background and text already carry that color (available as `var(--bn-tint)`), so another ring of it merges everything together, as observed on 2026-08-24. Choose a contrasting outline for depth; let the background and text convey the type.
contract.skin.13: Section navigation items. On wide screens these are **multi-line sidebar cards with an icon, title and description**; on narrow screens they are pill chips in a horizontal bar. Account for both forms. Defaults are transparent rows with a light tint when selected; use nav-item-active to emphasize selection.
contract.skin.14: Also applied to the selected navigation item, alongside nav-item. Put selected styles here; styling nav-item would highlight every item.
contract.skin.15: An item in a horizontal tab bar: main header navigation, in-page TabBar or scope bar. Short elements can use pill corners. Defaults are transparent text tabs with a solid fill or underline when selected.
contract.skin.16: Also applied to the selected tab, alongside tab. Some defaults use a solid accent background with white text. When overriding background, set color too, to avoid white text on white.
contract.skin.17: Candidate rows in dropdowns, command palettes, conversation/draft lists, font lists and search results. **These are not buttons**: solid backgrounds make menus look like stacks of buttons, which is why this family previously had no hook. Use a light tint or outline for definition.
contract.skin.18: Also applied to the selected candidate, alongside option. Put selected styles here, not on option. Some selected rows use **brand/platform colors** (provider cards and connection rows). Overriding their background is possible but removes provider identity; use outlines or shadows to preserve it.
contract.skin.19: The shared base for red failure, yellow partial-completion and empty-state notes. **This controls shape**: corners, outlines and shadows. Their colors already follow danger*/warning*/border palette tokens, so there is no need to redefine them here.
contract.skin.20: Also applied to red failure notes, alongside note. **These appear only on errors**; do not make them less noticeable than body text.
contract.skin.21: Also applied to yellow notes for work completed with exceptions, alongside note. Keep them visually distinct from note-danger; identical colors erase the difference in severity.
contract.skin.22: Also applied to empty-state notes, alongside note. **The dashed outline communicates emptiness**; a solid outline makes the empty state look like an actual card.
contract.skin.23: Dashed spaces for adding another item: subscription-grid cards, inline pills, “+ Add row” form controls and file upload areas. **Dashes communicate an empty slot**, as with note-empty. Do not turn it into a solid button with background. **Multiple shapes**: grid cards, full rows and compact buttons share this hook. Do not assume one shape; keep corner radii at or below 24px. Adjust border width/style/color and a light background, with a subtle hover tint.
contract.skin.24: Toggle track, usually the pink sliding switch. **Width and height are inline styles; setting them here has no effect**. This hook controls corners, outlines and shadows. Use separate backgrounds for off (here) and on (switch-on).
contract.skin.25: Also applied to enabled toggles, alongside switch. **On and off must be immediately distinguishable**. Identical backgrounds remove the distinction across the site; the default uses pink for on and gray for off.
contract.skin.26: The thumb inside the toggle track. If the track is made square, adjust the thumb too. **Do not set left/top/width/height**: these are inline motion values that cannot be overridden here.
contract.skin.27: Compact chips for filters, levels and toggles. They change values, not views (tabs change views). Shapes vary and space is often tight; use outline with a negative offset rather than a border that affects layout.
contract.skin.28: Also applied to selected/lit chips, alongside chip. **Only shape is customizable here**: corners, outline style, shadows and font weight. Selected backgrounds and borders use intentionally non-overridable inline semantic colors. Several chips may be active at once (log levels are multi-select); a background override would collapse debug/info/warn/error into one color. Do not set background; it has no effect. **Use `var(--bn-tint)` for the outline color**: each selected chip exposes its semantic color there. A fixed color with a negative outline-offset sits over the semantic border and makes all four levels look identical (observed on 2026-08-24).
